newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Upbeat Australian stocks bound to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Upbeat Australian stocks bound to higher close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2692 +38 US 30yr cl 6.48 -0.07
10yrbond futs 93.440 +0.095 Gold NY 318.05 Lon fix 319.50
*Stocks end off highs but solid gains locked away by close, offshore tone inspires local trade. Volume 352.75 million, value A$812.93 million, 1,095 stocks traded, 335 steady, 451 up, 309 down.

The Australian share market closed off its highs for the day but had still locked away solid gains by the close on Thursday as local traders took the bullish lead from record breaking runs in offshore markets.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 23.3 points to 2,669.7, having peaked late morning at 2,683.7 before sellers succumbed to the temptation to cash in some quick gains.
September share price index futures contracts were 38 points higher at 2,692, a 22.3 point premium to the underlying index.
"It's all been quite firm. We seem to have followed Wall Street again," said Robert Cameron of Cameron Securities.
A resurgent banking sector was one of best performers on the day, a stronger bond market helping boost the popular group.
ANZ Bank ended with the best gains of the big four, up 1.7 percent to A9.95, while Westpac Banking Corp also made good ground, climbing 1.1 percent to A$7.88.
Commonwealth Bank touched a record high at A$16.56 before easing to end up 14.5 cents at A$16.475, while sector heavyweight National Australia Bank rose 14 to A$19.26.
"The banking sector has returned to favour after a bit of profit taking earlier in the week," said Burrell and Co director, Derek Bond.
Gutnick-controlled Centaur Mining and Exploration NL added over 5.6 percent to A$1.50 amid rumours of an imminent bid for Great Central, the largest Gutnick firm.

Great Central, the centre of bid speculation with Canadian giant Barrick Gold Corp, ended seven cents lower at A$2.64 after hitting an early high of A$2.812, 34 percent higher than last week's low of A$2.10 after the bullion selloff.
Great Central's Jundee neighbour in Western Australia Eagle Mining NL made strong gains, up nearly seven percent to A$2.30.

Pay TV operator Australis Media made strong gains, ending 5.5 cents higher at 20 cents with an active 18.7 million shares traded, the bulk of them in one line of 10.5 million shares crossed though SBC Warburg.

Traders speculated that an announcement of a long mooted merger with rival operator Foxtel, jointly owned by News Corp and Telstra Corp, the government owned telecommunications carrier, may be imminent.
Automation software group Ci Technologies made a strong debut on the boards, ending at A$2.10, 60 cents up on its issue price of A$1.50.
Turnover was boosted by some big lines in Westfield Trust, with 20 million units worth A$55 million specialled through the market by midday. Its units ended up two at A$2.74.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
Futures trade was heavy with much of the day's strength supported by moves in the September SPI contract which had 11,134 contracts traded. Options trade, however, was slow.
In other local markets, Australian bond yields clung to their lows for most of the day after a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries and as the Australian dollar put in a minor rally.
By 4.50 p.m. (0650 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.56 percent, compared to Wednesday's 6.67 percent.

The Australian dollar edged cautiously higher to a daily peak of US$0.7375 in what dealers termed a technical reaction to a deeply oversold position. But by 4.50 p.m. (0650 GMT), it had faded to US$0.7360/65, having crept ahead from an early US$0.7345/50 and Wednesday's late US$0.7325/30, which had been its lowest local close since August 1995.
